thread:
jordan: Heads-up: after last night's egress tighten in us-west-2, a warm-pool batch failed to complete keystore handshakes. warm-pool stayed at 0/40 for ~30m.

viv: Can you share the node log snippet?

jordan: Sure:
```
2026-03-25T02:14:10Z gpu-node-7 keystore: decrypt err=KMS_DECRYPT_TIMEOUT attempt=4
2026-03-25T02:14:12Z gpu-node-7 http: POST https://audit-shipper.internal/v1/logs -> 403 Forbidden
```

harry: 403 on audit-shipper = worker egress path not allowed. We updated controlplane allowlist but the warmpool NAT ENIs are ephemeral and weren't auto-enrolled.

jordan: Impact: autoscaler rebalanced load to other regions for 30m, estimated extra egress ~$1.2k.

policy-bot: mitigation options: (1) revert egress deny, (2) add subnet CIDR allow, (3) detect NAT ENIs and add ENI-specific allow.

viv: Pick 3. We'll run a tiny lambda to discover current ENIs and apply a narrow allow for kms + audit endpoints for 2h. Also add alert: KMS 5xx >1% for 5m.

keystore-bot: sched:apply-allowlist --subnet subnet-warm-w2 --endpoints kms.us-west-2.redwood-internal,audit-shipper.internal --ttl 2h :white_check_mark:

jordan: Canary: 3/3 test nodes joined, decrypt.latency median dropped 2.0s -> 130ms. warming normalized.

harry: Long-term: propose static per-region ENIs for warm-pool or route keystore via controlplane egress. Draft RFC and firewall CI that simulates ephemeral ENI churn.

jordan: I'll open the postmortem, include compliance note for the temporary exception and the approver. Closing once RFC created.
